title: Objections to the immoral side of the music life
summary: Charles says he disliked bad behavior at parades and stag parties and prayed to be spared it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Oh, so I see. Well I had the opportunity to travel if I wanted to travel, but I didn't see that. I couldn't see travel. Because in other words, I was playing music, I loved music, I was crazy about music. But it looked like I can't stand foolishness. That's quite a humbug. You see, so there's two things. You can't serve but one master. That's right. You see. And as well as I used to, people used to say that I played an instrument, I satisfied the people. But it looked like I didn't like some of the action that went on during the music. Because you know, ain't nobody in the world going to do a thing and going to pray and ask God to deliver him for the good. Now just like when I used to play those parades. You know, it used to work on my nerves. Some of them women even with children on the side of their lap like that following the parade. You ever seen anything like that in your life? Oh yes. We've seen it. So usually I'm not exaggerating. Oh yes, sure.

But did they do? Well, it is. I mean, the people were just not acting. Like people who are well-raised, you know, with breeding and so on would act and he just didn't like it. Yeah, they were cut up at the parade. You saw all kind of things at the parade.

And another thing, people are dancing. Don't you think people should dance decently? Oh yes. And God said no matter what you're doing, if you're there you're a part of it. So you see, then I've seen myself playing music and didn't even see the people that I could hear them. Now you know, you know. That don't work.
Where was that you couldn't see the people? You mean you don't want to talk about that? No, no, no. You mean something pretty bad is going on.

I mean pretty bad going on is right. Now you got it. Now you're coming my way. I see. Now you're coming my way. I see. And then the other thing, I see myself playing engagement. Engagement, brother. And it's supposed to be a stag. And things went on that I didn't want to see even. Me myself didn't want to see. And I was a part of it. Now wouldn't you pray and ask God to deliver you from things like that? I've seen myself right at the restaurant on Boydman Street there, playing a stag there on the stand well. And I got to stand in front of pianists like that to keep off from seeing what was going on in the back of me.
Now you know that. You can't come tell me you like that kind of a life.

You know this is a picture I think that many people had gotten of all, of all, things that jazz people played for you see. And this is the thing that, I mean brought many of our jazz musicians in disrepute years ago. Because they were at things of this kind and they would be associated with the picture. That's right. You didn't have that at the Frans de Mille Hall though, or at the country club. No, no, no. They had that.
Well like I said, there's many good places. You can't disqualify all. Just now and then you run across those kind of things. That's right.
